claims.text: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has high caloric performance.
The unmodified alloy has poor mechanical integrity and tends to crack under load.
Adding a uniformly dispersed ductile, low-melting metallic phase will improve the alloy's mechanical integrity.
The added metallic phase will impede crack initiation.
The added metallic phase will impede crack propagation.
The composite will preserve the alloy's large caloric response under applied magnetic fields.
The composite will preserve the alloy's large caloric response under applied pressure fields.
An In-based alloy can provide a rare-earth-free, low-melting, ductile secondary phase.
Coherent or semi-coherent interfaces will form between the secondary phase and the high-entropy-alloy matrix.
The secondary-phase interfaces will improve load transfer.
The ductile phase will absorb energy during mechanical loading.
Energy absorption by the ductile phase will reduce stress concentrations near microstructural flaws.
Limiting the volume fraction of the secondary phase will minimize interference with the caloric phase transition.
The intervention will increase compressive strength by approximately 30–50% relative to the unmodified alloy.
The transition temperature will remain within approximately 10% of its baseline value.
The latent heat will remain within approximately 10% of its baseline value.
The entropy change will remain within approximately 10% of its baseline value.
The hypothesized behavior is expected under moderate field strengths and temperatures that activate the caloric response.
Very high temperatures could cause excessive softening of the ductile secondary phase.
Extreme loading regimes could cause phase separation of the ductile secondary phase.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines preservation as caloric metrics remaining within approximately 10% of baseline, but the falsification rule says that less than 10% degradation falsifies the hypothesis. Thus, successful caloric preservation would itself trigger falsification. The intended failure condition would instead be degradation greater than approximately 10%.
